Reference.description: A live value on the wire: one exported binding within one scope. It is the language's projection of the callable kind — what a value of a callable type is when it crosses the seam — and no family declares it or names it.

fields.name: binding
fields.description: The binding, minted by the scope that exported it and opaque to everyone else: the scope's own evidence of identity, epoch and freshness lives in here, so a representation from an ended scope cannot resolve in a new one.

fields.name: contract
fields.description: The declaration the binding implements, family/Type. It is nominal: a reference is usable exactly where the callable it was declared as is expected.

Invoke.description: One invocation of an exported binding.

fields.name: contract
fields.description: The declaration the caller believes the binding implements; a mismatch is refused before dispatch.

fields.name: request
fields.description: The callable's request, validated against the declared type; absent when the callable takes nothing.

fields.name: result
fields.description: The callable's result, validated against the declared type; absent when the callable answers nothing.

Release.description: Release of a binding: idempotent, and the same operation whether the releasing side exported it or imported it.

Released.description: What a release answers; it carries nothing, since release is idempotent and says nothing about what the binding did.
